entries.why_wrong: You're flagging a real style nitpick — `getBytes()` uses the platform default charset — but that's a portability concern, not what breaks when the disk is full. The actual failure is that a thrown `IOException` from `write()` skips `out.close()` entirely, leaking the descriptor regardless of what charset was used.

Unbuffered writes are a throughput concern, not a correctness one — `FileOutputStream` writing straight to the OS has nothing to do with what happens when disk space runs out. The real issue is that when `write()` throws, execution never reaches `out.close()`, so the file handle stays open no matter how fast or slow the writes were.

Calling `close()` twice wouldn't help — `close()` is idempotent and a single call already fully releases the stream. The bug is that `close()` never gets called at all when `write()` throws, because the code has no try/finally or try-with-resources to guarantee it runs on the error path.
